function: Debris detection and material classification from CSI by SVMs, a sensing task outside the seven areas. p. 3: "a second SVM model is employed to classify the type of debris"
notes: Reason function, shown on p. 3. Checks 1 to 4 pass: a research article that proposes and evaluates a method, whose learned components are two supervised RBF-kernel SVMs acting on physical-layer CSI (p. 3: "The extracted CSI features are input to a pre-trained SVM model for debris detection"; p. 8: "Our SVM models employ RBF kernels"). Their function, detecting debris and classifying its material (smooth glass or rough metal) from five statistics of the CSI magnitude (p. 3), is sensing and target classification, not the problem of any of the seven areas. Not area 5: the waveform is reused rather than designed (p. 2: "our system reuses the standard QPSK-modulated carrier signals"), no beam or resource is learned, and the adaptive MIMO, frequency, and power strategies of Section V.B are rule-based proposals without results (p. 12: "pre-computed look-up tables (LUTs)"). Not area 2: channel estimation is pilot-based MMSE (p. 3) and the simulations bypass it (p. 8: "our simulations assume perfect CSI knowledge at the receiver"). Not area 6: there is no learned power, resource, or beam control of the inter-satellite link. The link does communicate (QPSK, BER in Figs. 7 to 9, pp. 9-10, MIMO 4x4 to 64x64 in Table I, p. 8), so the listed example of sensing alone in a system that does not communicate does not apply literally; the reviewer may confirm that learned sensing inference in an ISAC link, without learned beams, waveforms, or resources, stays outside area 5.
